group: How much of each market is owned from abroad
title: How much of Brazil's shares and other equity is owned from abroad: non-residents and residents, in its own currency
short: Brazil shares and other equity, owned from abroad
source: OECD financial balance sheets, non-consolidated, quarterly (DSD_NASEC20@DF_T720R_Q), Brazil (BRA): issued by residents (sector S1, liabilities) and held by non-residents (S2, assets), shares and other equity (F51), national currency; residents = issued minus non-residents (our calculation). note: Each book splits everything residents of Brazil have issued of shares and other equity into the part held by non-residents, as the country reports it to the OECD, and the rest, held by residents (our calculation: issued minus non-residents), in its own currency and at market value. Non-residents means every holder outside the country, including foreign central banks and funds. It does not say which kind of resident holds the rest, which needs the country's own accounts. Brazil reports no listed-shares line to the OECD, so this is listed and unlisted shares and other equity together. Source: OECD.
